CJSModels

Fit first-capture-conditional Cormack-Jolly-Seber models in R using native TMB. Estimate unit-time apparent survival and detection from encounter histories.

Experimental software. Results are provisional. Development tests do not establish parameter recovery, interval coverage or scientific maturity. Apparent survival combines mortality and permanent emigration.

Start with a fixed-effects model

Read the worked example, then the data constructor and fitting function. Install from GitHub with remotes::install_github("itchyshin/CJSModels"), or from a reviewed local source checkout with R CMD INSTALL .; TMB and a C++ compiler are required. No CRAN release is claimed.

The likelihood conditions on each animal’s first capture. It excludes all-zero histories and does not estimate abundance or unseen animals.

Tested scope

The local R full check passed Status OK with 2,280 assertions and two explained finite-difference warnings. A fresh fixed-effects R/Julia fit agreed within coefficient 1e-5 and loglikelihood 1e-6 tolerances. These are bounded numerical and package checks, not all-route parity or scientific calibration.

Shared and persistent individual effects, process-specific SD predictors and reference-selection correction are inherited experimental routes. Their broad extraction-specific fit, output and interval combinations remain unqualified. Repeated-sampling recovery and interval coverage/calibration remain deferred. Shared-effect reference selection, shared-plus-individual combinations and random-effect or selection bridges are outside the current contract.

Julia companion

Read the Julia companion documentation.

CJSModels.jl provides a standalone Julia API. The optional R bridge uses a separate Julia environment containing CJSModels and RCall; RCall is not a dependency of the standalone Julia package. See bridge setup for the R entry point. Public development source is available on GitHub. The software remains experimental.
